lead_title: Part VII-only extraction misses filing-point identity evidence
observation: The existing person-role long table captured Part VII rows but not return-header BusinessOfficerGrp or BooksInCareOfDetail person strings.
why_unexpected: The five HR candidates had been framed mainly from Part VII exact/near names even though the inherited official XML contained additional identity-bearing fields.
next_test: Inspect only the five assigned candidates across inherited AWWA/OESC/KOSC/NOSCO XMLs and keep field semantics separate.
potential_value: May improve future person extraction by distinguishing tax-period roster roles from filing-point signers and books contacts.

lead_title: Header and books fields add exact names to two candidate chains
observation: AWWA FY2023 return header gives Brooke Epp/AWWA Treasurer and the same return gives Amber N Tracy in both InCareOfNm and BooksInCareOfDetail.
why_unexpected: These exact strings remove the earlier impression that 01a rested only on Epp versus Epps and that 01c began only with the later AWWA Part VII row.

potential_value: Can sharpen 01a and 01c while exposing a reusable schema distinction.

lead_title: Adjacent returns confirm that omitted fields change evidence strength
observation: AWWA FY2024 Part VII returns Brooke Epps and Amber Tracy; KOSC FY2024 header and FY2025 Part VII return Brooke Epp; OESC FY2023 header/Part VII return AMBER TRACY. This raises 01a and 01c to high-convergence candidates while preserving semantic cautions.

next_test: If later authorized open a separate ecology-wide extraction audit covering BusinessOfficerGrp, PrincipalOfficerNm, InCareOfNm and BooksInCareOfDetail with dated-role semantics.
potential_value: Could improve coverage reporting and prevent false person-network sparsity.
